'''Araceli Lopez-Martens''' (born 1971){{r|cd}} is a French [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] specializing in the [[Island of stability|stability]] of [[superheavy element]]s, and known for her research on the [[superdeformation]] of nuclei and her role in the discovery of <sup>249</sup>No, the lightest [[Isotopes of nobelium|isotope of nobelium]]. She is a director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]].{{r|silver}}

==Education and career==
Lopez-Martens was born in 1971. After primary and secondary education in France, she studied physics and Russian at the [[University of Sussex]] in England from 1989 to 1993, before returning to France for a [[diplôme d'études approfondies]] and doctoral thesis in physics through [[Paris-Sud University]] and the Centre de Sciences Nucléaires et de Sciences de la Matière in 1994 and 1996, respectively.{{r|cd|timeworld}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Étude de la désexcitation des états superdéformés dans la région de masse <math display="inline">a=190</math>'', was directed by Fazia Hannachi.{{r|these}}

After completing her doctorate, she became a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] in Denmark.{{r|timeworld}} 
She has worked as a researcher for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) since 1999,{{r|orcid}} initially at the [[Hubert Curien Pluridisciplinary Institute|Institut de Recherches Subatomiques]] (IReS) in [[Strasbourg]],{{r|timeworld}} and is currently a director of research for the CNRS, affiliated with the Laboratory of the Physics of the two Infinities – Irène Joliot-Curie, jointly operated by the CNRS, [[Paris-Saclay University]], and the [[Université Paris Cité]].{{r|silver}}

Her research has involved participation in the international collaborations on the Euroball gamma detector array, the [[AGATA (gamma-ray detector)|AGATA]] advanced gamma tracking array, and the S3 Super Separator Spectrometer at the [[Grand Accélérateur National d'Ions Lourds]] (GANIL) in France.{{r|silver}}

==Recognition==
Lopez-Martens received the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2023.{{r|silver}}
